# Legacy factory compatibility (PHP migration)

Scenario v2 does not use factories. Author new integrations with ordinary code inside `Autonoma\Sdk\Scenario::defineScenario` as described in `implement.md` and `scenarios.md`.

This page exists only for projects migrating older customer code that already calls `Autonoma\Sdk\Factory::define`. The helper is not registered with the handler, is not discoverable, and is never invoked by the v2 protocol. Do not introduce it in a new v2 integration.

The method is `Factory::define` (not `defineFactory`).

## Temporary use during migration

Existing helper calls may remain temporarily while their creation and cleanup behavior moves into scenario-owned functions. New v2 code should call those functions directly from `up` and `down`.

## The shape

```php
use Autonoma\Sdk\Factory;
use Autonoma\Sdk\Types\FactoryContext;

$userFactory = Factory::define(
    create: function (array $data, FactoryContext $ctx): array {
        $user = User::create($data);
        return ['id' => $user->id, 'email' => $user->email];
    },
    teardown: function (array $record, FactoryContext $ctx): void {
        User::destroy($record['id']);
    },
);
```

`Factory::define(callable $create, ?callable $teardown = null, array $inputFields = []): FactoryDefinition`:

- `create(array $data, FactoryContext $ctx)` runs your real creation code and must return an array with at least an `'id'` key.
- `teardown(array $record, FactoryContext $ctx)` optionally deletes the record. Omit it and the factory creates but does not delete.
- `inputFields` is an optional array of field declarations for the host's own validation; it is not enforced by the SDK.

`FactoryContext` has three readonly fields: `$ctx->refs`, `$ctx->scenarioName`, and `$ctx->testRunId`.

## Using a factory from a scenario

A factory is a plain `FactoryDefinition` object whose `create`/`teardown` are callables you invoke yourself; wire its output into your scenario's `teardown` so `down` can undo it.

```php
use Autonoma\Sdk\Scenario;
use Autonoma\Sdk\Types\FactoryContext;
use Autonoma\Sdk\Types\ScenarioUpContext;
use Autonoma\Sdk\Types\ScenarioUpResult;
use Autonoma\Sdk\Types\ScenarioDownContext;

Scenario::defineScenario(
    name: 'with-user',
    description: 'One user created through the user factory',
    up: function (ScenarioUpContext $ctx) use ($userFactory): ScenarioUpResult {
        $fctx = new FactoryContext(refs: [], scenarioName: 'with-user', testRunId: $ctx->testRunId);
        $user = ($userFactory->create)(['email' => "u+{$ctx->testRunId}@example.com"], $fctx);
        return new ScenarioUpResult(
            teardown: ['user' => $user],
        );
    },
    down: function (ScenarioDownContext $ctx) use ($userFactory): void {
        if ($userFactory->teardown !== null) {
            $fctx = new FactoryContext(refs: [], scenarioName: $ctx->name, testRunId: $ctx->testRunId);
            ($userFactory->teardown)($ctx->teardown['user'], $fctx);
        }
    },
);
```

Because `create`/`teardown` live on the `FactoryDefinition` as callable properties, invoke them with `($userFactory->create)(...)` / `($userFactory->teardown)(...)`. Most scenarios never need this - a few lines of direct creation code in `up` and the matching deletes in `down` are usually clearer.
